column3: It's a great day to fall in love all over again.
column4: “今天真是重新坠入爱河的好日子。”

column3: People do get so carried away sometimes, but not I.
column4: “人有时会忘乎所以，但我不会。”

column3: Sometimes I just don't like somebody.
How can someone be so consumed by hate?
column4: “一个人怎么会被仇恨吞噬到这种地步？”

column3: I don't understand how somebody can become so obsessed by what somebody else has.
column4: “我不明白，一个人怎么会如此执着于别人拥有的东西。”

column3: Is there something to be happy about?
It really gets me down sometimes.
How can people be so glum?
I have trouble controlling my temper.
People can be so angry, and I just don't understand it.
column4: “人怎么会有那么大的怒气，我实在不理解。”

column3: W... worried?  Do I look worried?
There's nothing to be upset about.
I just don't understand these flames of passion people go on about.
column4: “人们总说欲火难耐，我实在无法理解。”

column3: I'm at my best under pressure.
column4: “有压力时，我反而发挥得最好。”

column3: Yes, I want more.  Is that so bad?
column4: “是，我想要更多。这有那么糟吗？”

column3: Why are they so fixated on these baubles?
column4: “他们为什么如此痴迷这些小玩意？”

column3: I could really use a drink.
Sometimes I think I need a drink, but I can control myself.
column4: “有时我觉得该喝一杯，但我能克制自己。”

column3: I am not governed by urges.
There's nothing like a good brawl.
column4: “没有什么比得上痛快打上一架。”

column3: Why must they be so violent?
Get me going and I won't stop for anything.
column4: “只要我行动起来，就没有什么能让我停下。”

column3: Maybe I give up too early sometimes.
I don't always do things in the most efficient way.
column4: “我做事并不总是那么有效率。”

column3: We must be careful not to waste.
I don't mind stirring things up.
It's so great when everybody just gets along.
You don't care, so don't ask.
I try to live and behave properly.
column4: “我尽量让生活和言行合乎规矩。”
“所谓合乎规矩的生活，究竟是什么？”

column3: I was never one to follow advice.
I'm not much of a decision maker.
Bravery is not a strength of mine.
I don't think I'm cut out for this.
column4: “我觉得自己不适合做这件事。”

column3: Some people are so wrapped up in themselves.
My goals are important to me.
I don't feel like I need to chase anything.
column4: “我觉得自己没有什么非追求不可的东西。”

column3: One should always return a favor.
It's not a gift if you expect something in return.
column4: “若是指望回报，那就不算馈赠。”

column3: I wouldn't feel comfortable getting all dressed up.
column4: “打扮得太讲究，会让我不自在。”

column3: Did you hear the one about the
Don't get on my bad side.
You shouldn't waste your life on revenge.
I am a very, very important person.
column4: “我是个非常、非常重要的人物。”

column3: There's no room for mercy in this world.
Show some mercy now and again.
I'm feeling optimistic about the future.
I don't really want to know.
I don't feel like telling you about it.
I could tell you all about it!
column4: “我可以把来龙去脉都告诉你！”

column3: If you have a task, do it properly.
It's not perfect, but it's good enough.  Why fret about it?
column4: “虽然不完美，但已经够好了，何必为此烦恼？”

column3: I'm not going to change my mind.
Try to keep an open mind.
Everybody has their own way of life.
I don't understand why they have to be that way.
column4: “我不理解，他们为什么非要那样。”

column3: I don't really get attached to people.
I go with the flow sometimes.
Don't bother trying to play on my emotions.
I don't like being obligated to anybody.
Oh, I don't usually think much.
One must always carefully consider the correct course of action.
column4: “做事之前，总应慎重考虑怎样才妥当。”

column3: Everything just so in its proper place!
My trust is earned, and not by many.
column4: “想得到我的信任，得有真凭实据，而做到的人不多。”

column3: It's such a joy to be with people.
I prefer to be by myself.
People should listen to what I have to say.
There's so much to be done!
I need some more excitement in my life.
I'd just as soon not have anything too exciting happen today.
column4: “我倒希望今天别发生什么太刺激的事。”

column3: Do you have dreams?  Tell me a story!
Try to focus on the practical side of the matter.
column4: “尽量多考虑事情实际的一面。”

column3: I encountered a fascinating conundrum recently.
column4: “我最近遇到了一个引人入胜的难题。”

column3: A great piece of art is one that moves me.
I guess I just don't appreciate art.
I'm feel like I'm about to snap.
Everything is all piling up at once!
column4: “所有事情一下子全压过来了！”

column3: I cannot stand the world any longer...
I feel angry all the time.
I can't take much more of this!
I feel so tired of everything.
It's all starting to get me down.
Society flourishes when law breakers are punished.
column4: “违法者受到惩罚，社会才能兴盛。”

column3: One should always respect the law.
No law can do justice to the complexity of life.
column4: “生活如此复杂，没有哪条法律能面面俱到。”

column3: Nothing gives them the right to establish these laws.
column4: “他们根本无权制定这些法律。”

column3: I consider laws to be more of a suggestion than anything.
column4: “在我看来，法律更像是一种建议。”

column3: Rules are there to be bent, but they shouldn't be flouted thoughtlessly.
column4: “规矩可以变通，却不该不加思索地违背。”

column3: Some laws are just, while others were made to be broken.
column4: “有些法律公正合理，有些却注定要被打破。”

column3: One must always be loyal to their cause and the ones they serve.
column4: “忠于自己的事业，也忠于自己追随的人。”

column3: How can society function without loyalty?  We must be able to have faith in each other.
column4: “没有忠诚，社会如何维系？我们必须彼此信任。”

column3: You must never forget true loyalty.  Repay it in full.
column4: “真正的忠诚不可辜负，应当全心回报。”

column3: Never lose yourself in loyalty.  You know what is best for yourself.
column4: “不要因忠诚迷失自己。你自己知道什么对你最好。”

column3: The whole idea of loyalty is pointless.  Acting purely out of loyalty implies acting against one's own best interest.
column4: “忠诚这个念头毫无意义。只凭忠诚行事，就意味着违背自己的最大利益。”

column3: Don't serve anyone blindly.  You'll only get into trouble.
column4: “不要盲目效忠任何人，那只会惹祸上身。”

column3: Consider your loyalties carefully, adhere to them while they last, and abandon them when you must.
column4: “慎重选择效忠的对象，该坚守时坚守，必须放弃时就放弃。”

column3: You should only maintain loyalty so long as something more important is not at stake.
column4: “忠诚应当坚守，但不能为此危及更重要的事。”

column3: Loyalty has value, but you should always keep the broader picture in mind.
column4: “忠诚固然可贵，但也要顾全大局。”

column3: Family is the true bond that keeps society thriving.
column4: “家庭才是维系社会兴盛的纽带。”

column3: You can always rely on your family when everything else falls away.
column4: “纵然失去一切，你仍然可以依靠家人。”

column3: How great it is to be surrounded by family!
I hold the relationships I've forged myself over family ties I had no part in creating.
column4: “比起生来就有的亲缘，我更看重自己建立的关系。”

column3: We cannot choose our families, but we can choose to avoid them.
column4: “我们无法选择家人，却可以选择远离他们。”

column3: I was always irritated by family.
You can't always rely on your family, but it's good to know somebody is there.
column4: “家人未必总能靠得住，但知道有人在，总是好的。”

column3: Family is complicated and those ties be both a boon and a curse.  Sometimes both at once!
column4: “家庭关系复杂，可能是福，也可能是祸，有时两者兼有！”

column3: When all other bonds wither, friendship will remain.
column4: “纵使其他情分都淡去，友谊仍会长存。”

column3: Surround yourself with friends you can trust and you will be unstoppable.
column4: “有值得信赖的朋友相伴，就没有什么能阻挡你。”

column3: There's nothing like a good friend.
column4: “没有什么比得上一个好朋友。”

column3: Building friendships is a waste.  There is no bond that can withstand distance or a change of circumstance.
column4: “结交朋友是白费心力。没有哪份情谊经得起相隔遥远或境遇变迁。”

column3: Friends are future enemies.  I don't see the difference.  People do as they must.
column4: “朋友终会成为敌人，两者并无区别。人各有不得已。”

column3: Be careful of your so-called friends.
Friends are nice, but you should keep your priorities straight.
column4: “有朋友是好事，但也要分清轻重。”

column3: You can be powerful or powerless.  The choice is yours, until somebody makes it for you.
column4: “你可以掌握权力，也可以任人摆布。在别人替你决定之前，选择权在你手中。”

column3: Power over others is the only true measure of worth.
column4: “能支配多少人，才是衡量价值的唯一标准。”

column3: It is abhorrent to seek power over other people.
column4: “谋求支配他人的权力，令人不齿。”

column3: There's nothing admirable about bullying others.
column4: “欺凌他人，没有什么值得称道的。”

column3: The struggle for power must be balanced by other considerations.
column4: “争取权力时，也必须顾及其他事情。”

column3: Everything is so much easier when you just tell the truth.
There is nothing so important that it is worth telling a lie.
column4: “没有什么事重要到值得为它说谎。”

column3: You should always tell the truth.
Don't think about the truth, whatever that is.  Just say what needs to be said.
column4: “不必琢磨什么才是真相，说该说的话就好。”

column3: Is there ever a time when honesty by itself overrides other considerations?  Say what is right, not what is true.
column4: “难道诚实就能凌驾于一切考量之上？要说合适的话，而不只是真话。”

column3: There is no value in telling the truth thoughtlessly.  Consider the circumstances and say what is best.
column4: “不假思索地说实话没有意义。要看清情形，说最合适的话。”

column3: Sometimes the blunt truth just does more damage.  Think about how the situation will unfold before you speak.
column4: “有时直言实情只会造成更大伤害。开口之前，先想想后果。”

column3: It is best not to complicate your life with lies, sure, but the truth also has its problems.
column4: “最好别让谎言把生活弄复杂，但实话也有实话的麻烦。”

column3: There are times when it is alright not to tell the whole truth.
column4: “有时候，不把实情全说出来也无妨。”

column3: I do admire a clever trap.
There's no value in all of this scheming I see these days.
column4: “眼下这些勾心斗角，在我看来毫无价值。”

column3: Be shrewd, but do not lose yourself in guile.
column4: “处世要精明，却别迷失于算计。”

column3: I can appreciate the right turn of phrase.
column4: “恰到好处的措辞，我是懂得欣赏的。”

column3: I do admire a clever turn of phrase.
They are so full of all those big words.
column4: “他们满口都是装腔作势的大词。”

column3: Who are these mealy-mouthed cowards trying to impress?
column4: “这些说话拐弯抹角的懦夫，究竟想讨好谁？”

column3: There is a time for artful speech, and a time for blunt speech as well.
column4: “有时说话需要技巧，有时也该直言不讳。”

column3: Don't be afraid to do anything to get ahead in this world.
column4: “要在这世上出人头地，就别怕不择手段。”

column3: Life isn't fair, and sometimes you have to do what you have to do, but working toward a balance isn't a bad thing.
column4: “生活并不公平，有时也不得不如此，但尽力求个公道总不是坏事。”

column3: What do you care how I speak or how I live?
column4: “我怎么说话、怎么生活，关你什么事？”

column3: I can see a place for maintaining decorum, but it's exhausting to live that way.
column4: “我明白守礼有它的道理，但那样生活实在太累。”

column3: It's admirable when the traditions are upheld.
We need to move beyond traditions.
We need to find a better way than those of before.
column4: “我们需要找到比前人更好的办法。”

column3: Some traditions are worth keeping, but we should consider their overall value.
column4: “有些传统值得保留，但也应衡量它们整体的价值。”

column3: The creative impulse is so valuable.

column4: “艺术？倒不如说是在浪费大好机会。”

column3: Art is complicated.  I know what I like, but some I can do without.
column4: “艺术很复杂。我知道自己喜欢什么，有些则有也好，没有也罢。”

column3: It's better to work alone when possible, I think.  Cooperation breeds weakness.
column4: “我觉得能独自做事就独自做，合作只会让人软弱。”

column3: You should think carefully before embarking on a joint enterprise, though there is some value in working together.
column4: “合作虽有益处，但与人共事之前，还是应当仔细考虑。”

column3: Nobody is free, and it is pointless to act as if you are.
column4: “没有人是自由的，装作自由也毫无意义。”

column3: Personal freedom must be tempered by other considerations.
column4: “个人自由也必须有所节制，兼顾其他事情。”

column3: One should not complain or betray any feeling.
column4: “人不应抱怨，也不应流露任何情绪。”

column3: Do not hide yourself behind an unfeeling mask.
column4: “不要把自己藏在冷漠的面具后面。”

column3: There are times when it is best to keep your feelings to yourself, but I wouldn't want to force it.
column4: “有时把感受留在心里更好，但我不愿勉强。”

column3: The quest for knowledge never ends.
All of that so-called knowledge doesn't mean a thing.
column4: “那些所谓的知识，全都毫无意义。”

column3: Knowledge can be useful, but it can also be pointless or even dangerous.
column4: “知识可以有用，也可能毫无意义，甚至带来危险。”

column3: It is important to discover yourself.
Why would I waste time thinking about myself?
column4: “我为什么要浪费时间琢磨自己？”

column3: Some time spent in reflection is admirable, but you must not forget to live your life.
column4: “花些时间自省值得称道，但也别忘了好好生活。”

column3: I think self-control is key.  Master yourself.
column4: “我认为自制最为关键，要能掌控自己。”

column3: Why deny yourself your heart's desire?
People should be able to control themselves, but it's fine to follow impulses that aren't too harmful.
column4: “人应当懂得自制，但顺从一些无伤大雅的冲动也无妨。”

column3: The mind thinks best when the world is at rest.
Give me the bustle and noise over all that quiet!
column4: “比起一片寂静，我更喜欢喧闹与忙碌！”

column3: I like a balance of tranquility and commotion myself.
column4: “我喜欢宁静与热闹各占几分。”

column3: We should all be as one.  Why all the struggling?
column4: “我们本应同心同德，何必争斗不休？”

column3: We grow through debate and struggle, even chaos and discord.
column4: “我们在辩论与抗争中成长，甚至混乱与不和也能促人成长。”

column3: Some discord is a healthy part of society, but we must also try to live together.
column4: “社会中有些分歧未必是坏事，但我们也得努力相处。”

column3: It's great when we all get a chance to be merry together.
column4: “大家能聚在一起欢乐，真是美好！”

column3: Bah!  I hope you aren't celebrating something.
I can take or leave merrymaking myself, but I don't begrudge people their enjoyment.
column4: “我对玩乐可有可无，但也不反对别人享受快乐。”

column3: An artisan, their materials and the tools to shape them!
column4: “工匠、材料，还有将材料塑造成形的工具，多么美妙！”

column3: A tool should get the job done, but one shouldn't obsess over the details.
column4: “工具能把活干好就行，不必执着于细枝末节。”

column3: A skilled warrior is a beautiful sight to behold.
column4: “武艺高强的战士，令人赏心悦目。”

column3: Why this obsession with weapons and battle?  I don't understand some people.
column4: “为什么如此痴迷武器与战斗？有些人真让我不理解。”

column3: The world isn't always safe.  I can see the value in martial training, the beauty even, but it shouldn't be exalted.
column4: “这世界并不总是安全的。我明白习武的价值，甚至它的美，但不该将它奉为至高。”

column3: The amount of practice that goes into mastering a skill is so impressive.
column4: “精通一门技艺所付出的磨炼，实在令人敬佩。”

column3: We should all be so lucky as to truly master a skill.
column4: “但愿我们都能有幸真正精通一门技艺。”

column3: All of that practice is misspent effort.
Everyone should broaden their horizons.  Any work beyond learning the basics is just a waste.
column4: “人人都应拓宽眼界。掌握基础之后再花功夫，只是浪费。”

column3: There's more to life than becoming great at just one thing, but being good at several isn't bad!
column4: “人生不只有精通一件事，多擅长几样也不错！”

column3: I think people should hone their skills, but it's possible to take it too far and lose sight of the breadth of life.
column4: “人应当磨炼技艺，但太过投入，也会忽略生活的广阔。”

column3: The best way to get what you want out of life is to work for it.
column4: “想过上自己要的生活，最好的办法就是为之努力。”

column3: Hard work is the true sign of character.
In life, you should work hard.  Then work harder.
column4: “人生在世，应当努力，再更加努力。”

column3: Hard work is bested by luck, connections and wealth every time.
column4: “苦干从来比不上运气、人脉与财富。”

column3: You shouldn't whittle your life away on working.
column4: “不该把一生都消磨在劳作上。”

column3: It's foolish to work hard for anything.
column4: “为任何事辛苦劳作，都是愚蠢的。”

column3: Hard work is great.  Finding a way to work half as hard is even better.
column4: “勤劳固然好，找到省一半力气的办法更好。”

column3: I only work so hard, but sometimes you have to do what you have to do.
column4: “我干活只肯出这么多力，但有些事该做还是得做。”

column3: An earnest effort at any required tasks.  That's all that's needed.
column4: “把该做的事认真做完，就够了。”

column3: We must be ready to sacrifice when the time comes.
column4: “到了需要的时候，我们必须甘愿牺牲。”

column3: Why harm yourself for anybody else's benefit?
column4: “何必为了别人的好处损害自己？”

column3: Some self-sacrifice is worthy, but do not forget yourself in devotion to the well-being of others.
column4: “适当牺牲自己值得敬重，但为他人谋福祉，也别忘了自己。”

column3: It's a competitive world, and you'd be a fool to think otherwise.
column4: “这世界处处都是竞争，不承认这一点才是愚蠢。”

column3: All of this striving against one another is so foolish.
column4: “这些相互争胜的举动，实在愚蠢。”

column3: There is value in a good rivalry, but such danger as well.
column4: “有个好对手固然可贵，但竞争也暗藏危险。”

column3: Anybody that sticks to something a moment longer than they have to is an idiot.
column4: “没必要再坚持，却还多耗一刻的人，都是傻子。”

column3: It's good to keep pushing forward, but sometimes you just have to know when it's time to stop.
column4: “不断向前固然好，但有时也要懂得适可而止。”

column3: It's best to slow down and just relax.
Wouldn't it be grand to just take my life off and do nothing for the rest of my days?
column4: “若能从此歇下，余生什么也不做，岂不美好？”

column3: Time spent in leisure is such a waste.
There's some value in leisure, but one also has to engage with other aspects of life.
column4: “闲暇有其益处，但生活的其他方面也不能荒废。”

column3: Trade is the life-blood of a thriving society.
All of this buying and selling isn't honest work.
column4: “这些买进卖出的营生，算不上踏实劳动。”

column3: There's something to be said for trade as a necessity, but there are better things in life to do with one's time.
column4: “贸易确有必要，但人生还有更值得花时间的事。”

column3: There's nothing like a great romance!
column4: “没有什么比得上一场美好的爱情！”

column3: These people carrying on about romance should be more practical.
column4: “这些满口爱情的人，该实际一点。”

column3: You shouldn't get too carried away with romance, but it's fine in moderation.
column4: “别为爱情过于忘形，适度就好。”

column3: It's wonderful to be out exploring the wilds!
I could do without all of those creatures and that tangled greenery.
column4: “那些生物和纠缠的草木，我宁可都不要。”

column3: Nature can be enjoyed and used for myriad purposes, but there must always be respect and even fear of its power.
column4: “自然可供欣赏，也有无数用途，但对它的力量，始终要怀有尊重，乃至畏惧。”

column3: Let there be peace throughout the world.
How I long for the beautiful spectacle of war!
column4: “我多么向往战争那壮美的景象！”

column3: War is sometimes necessary, but peace must be valued as well, when we can have it.
column4: “战争有时不可避免，但能享有和平时，也应当珍惜。”
